questions.questionText: A good hypothesis is one that can be:
questions.explanation: Testable hypothesis = verifiable by experiment.

questions.questionText: To reduce random errors in an experiment, you should:
questions.explanation: Multiple readings + averaging reduces random error.

questions.questionText: In science, before publication, research is usually:
questions.explanation: Peer review = other scientists evaluate work.

questions.questionText: Number 0.00450 in scientific notation is:
questions.explanation: 0.00450 = 4.50 × 10⁻³ (move decimal 3 places left).

questions.questionText: Interpolating on a graph means:

options.a: Estimating a value WITHIN the data range
options.c: Reading off only the last point

questions.explanation: Interpolation = estimating within range. Extrapolation = outside range.

questions.questionText: A good data table should have:
questions.explanation: Tables need headings + units for clarity.

questions.questionText: A control group in an experiment is used to:
questions.explanation: Control = baseline (no treatment changed) for comparison.

questions.questionText: Repeating an experiment multiple times is called:
questions.explanation: Replication = repeating trials for reliability.

questions.questionText: In random sampling, every member of the population:
questions.explanation: Random sampling = equal chance for all.

questions.questionText: A bias in an experiment is:

options.a: A systematic error that distorts results

questions.explanation: Bias = systematic error (one direction).

questions.questionText: Operationalizing a variable means:
questions.explanation: Operationalize = define how to measure (e.g., 'plant height in cm').

questions.questionText: An observation is:
questions.explanation: Observation = directly using senses. Inference = conclusion from data.

questions.questionText: The cell membrane is:
questions.explanation: Selective permeability = some substances pass, others don't.

questions.questionText: Osmosis is the movement of:
questions.explanation: Osmosis = water movement across semi-permeable membrane.

questions.questionText: Diffusion is the movement of particles:
questions.explanation: Diffusion = passive movement from high to low concentration.

questions.questionText: Active transport requires:
questions.explanation: Active transport = against gradient = needs ATP energy.

questions.questionText: Plant cell walls contain:
questions.explanation: Plant cell walls = cellulose. Fungi = chitin. Bacteria = peptidoglycan.

questions.questionText: The cytoplasm in a cell is:

options.a: Jelly-like substance where organelles are found

questions.explanation: Cytoplasm = jelly-like fluid containing organelles.

questions.questionText: Plant cells typically have:

options.a: A large central vacuole for storage

questions.explanation: Plant cells have large central vacuole (stores water/nutrients).

questions.questionText: Ribosomes are found:

options.a: Free in cytoplasm and on rough ER

questions.explanation: Ribosomes = free in cytoplasm OR attached to rough ER.

questions.questionText: The Golgi apparatus is responsible for:
questions.explanation: Golgi = packaging and modifying proteins for export.

questions.questionText: The endoplasmic reticulum (ER) functions in:
questions.explanation: ER = protein synthesis (rough ER) and lipid synthesis (smooth ER).

questions.questionText: Lysosomes contain:

options.a: Digestive enzymes to break down waste

questions.explanation: Lysosomes = 'garbage disposal' = digestive enzymes.

questions.questionText: As a cell grows larger, its volume:
questions.explanation: Volume grows as cube of size; surface area as square → volume grows faster.

questions.questionText: Food energy is usually measured in:
questions.explanation: Food energy = kcal (1 kcal = 4184 J).

questions.questionText: Which is NOT a major food group?
questions.explanation: Plastic is not a food. Vegetables, fruits, grains are food groups.

questions.questionText: BMR (basal metabolic rate) is the energy:

options.a: Used at rest to maintain body functions

questions.explanation: BMR = minimum energy at rest for body functions.

questions.questionText: Generally, calorie needs are highest during:
questions.explanation: Adolescence = rapid growth = high calorie needs.

questions.questionText: Daily recommended water intake is approximately:
questions.explanation: ~2 L/day recommended (varies by activity).

questions.questionText: Excessive salt intake can lead to:
questions.explanation: High salt → high BP (cardiovascular risk).

questions.questionText: Natural sugar in fruit differs from added sugar because:

options.a: Natural sugar comes with fiber and nutrients

questions.explanation: Natural sugar in fruit = with fiber/vitamins. Added sugar = empty calories.

questions.questionText: Dietary fiber helps prevent:
questions.explanation: Fiber = aids digestion = prevents constipation.

questions.questionText: Antioxidants in food help:

options.a: Protect cells from damage by free radicals

questions.explanation: Antioxidants = neutralize free radicals = protect cells.

questions.questionText: On a food label, the 'serving size' is:
questions.explanation: Serving size = one recommended portion.

questions.questionText: Hard water contains high amounts of:
questions.explanation: Hard water = Ca²⁺ and Mg²⁺ ions.

questions.questionText: Which method can remove BOTH dissolved and undissolved impurities?
questions.explanation: Distillation removes both (evaporates + condenses).

questions.questionText: A hydrated salt contains:

options.a: Water molecules in its crystal structure

questions.explanation: Hydrated salt = water of crystallization (e.g., CuSO4·5H2O).

questions.questionText: A solubility curve that slopes UPWARD with temperature means:
questions.explanation: Upward slope = solubility increases with temperature (typical for solids).

questions.questionText: Unlike most solids, the solubility of gases in water usually:
questions.explanation: Gas solubility DECREASES with temperature (opposite of solids).

questions.questionText: When hydrated copper sulfate is heated, it:
questions.explanation: Hydrated CuSO4 loses water → white anhydrous form.

questions.questionText: Most nitrates and sodium salts are:
questions.explanation: General solubility rules: nitrates + sodium salts = soluble.

questions.questionText: ppm stands for:
questions.explanation: ppm = parts per million (concentration unit).

questions.questionText: A salt solution conducts electricity because:

options.a: It contains free ions that move

questions.explanation: Conductivity requires free-moving ions (electrolytes).

questions.questionText: In simple distillation, water vapor is:
questions.explanation: Distillation = evaporate + condense on cold surface.

questions.questionText: In the water cycle, water returns to land by:
questions.explanation: Water cycle: evaporation → condensation → precipitation.

questions.questionText: Eutrophication in water bodies is caused by:
questions.explanation: Eutrophication = excess nutrients → algal bloom → oxygen depletion.

questions.questionText: A more concentrated acid reacts:
questions.explanation: Higher concentration = more particles = faster/vigorous reaction.

questions.questionText: A buffer solution:

options.a: Resists pH change when small acid/base added

questions.explanation: Buffer resists pH change (e.g., blood plasma).

questions.questionText: Before using a pH meter, you should:
questions.explanation: Calibration with known pH buffers ensures accuracy.

questions.questionText: To test if a solution is acidic, you should dip:

options.a: Blue litmus paper into the solution

questions.explanation: Blue litmus → red = acidic solution.

questions.questionText: To test an UNKNOWN solution's pH, you should use:
questions.explanation: Universal indicator covers full pH range (1-14).

questions.questionText: 25 cm³ of 0.1 M HCl neutralizes 25 cm³ of:
questions.explanation: Equal volumes + equal concentrations = neutralization 1:1.

questions.questionText: When CO₂ dissolves in water, it forms:
questions.explanation: CO₂ + H₂O → H₂CO₃ (weak carbonic acid).

questions.questionText: Adding lime (Ca(OH)₂) to acidic soil:
questions.explanation: Lime (alkali) neutralizes soil acidity.

questions.questionText: HCl in the stomach helps to:
questions.explanation: Stomach HCl = kills pathogens + activates pepsin for digestion.

questions.questionText: Why is NaOH used in drain cleaners?

options.a: It dissolves grease and hair (strong base)

questions.explanation: NaOH (strong base) dissolves organic clogs (grease, hair).

questions.questionText: Acid rain damages limestone statues because:
questions.explanation: H₂SO₄/HNO₃ + CaCO₃ → erosion of limestone/marble.

questions.questionText: Traditional soap is made by reacting fat with:
questions.explanation: Soap = fat + NaOH (saponification).

questions.questionText: In a closed system, total momentum:
questions.explanation: Law of conservation of momentum: total momentum is conserved.

questions.questionText: If force on 2 kg object is 10 N, acceleration is:
A car slows from 30 m/s to 10 m/s in 4 s. Deceleration =
questions.explanation: a = (10-30)/4 = -20/4 = -5 m/s². Deceleration = 5 m/s².

questions.questionText: A horizontal line on a distance-time graph means:
questions.explanation: Horizontal line = no change in distance = stationary.

questions.questionText: A horizontal line on a velocity-time graph means:
questions.explanation: Horizontal v-t = constant velocity = zero acceleration.

questions.questionText: Velocity changes from 5 m/s to 15 m/s in 2 s. Acceleration =
To produce 4 m/s² acceleration on 5 kg mass, force =
Weight of 5 kg object on Earth (g=10):
Pressure = Force / Area. If F=20N, A=4 m², P =
Friction force between two surfaces depends on:
questions.explanation: Friction depends on surface roughness + normal force (F = μN).

questions.questionText: In a reflection experiment, the angle of incidence equals:

options.a: Angle of reflection (both measured from normal)

questions.explanation: Law of reflection: angle of incidence = angle of reflection.

questions.questionText: Refractive index n = c/v. If c=3×10⁸ and v=2×10⁸, n =
Snell's law is expressed as:

options.a: n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂

questions.explanation: Snell's law: n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂.

questions.questionText: Critical angle occurs when:
questions.explanation: Critical angle = incident angle when refracted ray = 90°.

questions.questionText: Total internal reflection occurs when:

options.a: Light goes from denser to less dense medium at angle > critical angle
options.b: Light goes from less dense to denser

questions.explanation: TIR: denser to less dense at/beyond critical angle.

questions.questionText: A magnifying glass produces a:
questions.explanation: Magnifying glass = convex lens = virtual upright magnified image.

questions.questionText: A spectroscope separates light into:
questions.explanation: Spectroscope splits light into its spectrum by wavelength.

questions.questionText: Red, green, and blue are:
questions.explanation: RGB = additive primaries (light mixing).

questions.questionText: A pinhole camera produces an image that is:
questions.explanation: Pinhole camera = real, inverted image (light passes through small hole).

questions.questionText: A periscope uses two mirrors to:
questions.explanation: Periscope = two mirrors at 45° to redirect light around obstacles.

questions.questionText: A rainbow is formed by:

options.a: Dispersion and internal reflection in water droplets

questions.explanation: Rainbow = dispersion + reflection inside raindrops.

questions.questionText: A mirage in a desert is caused by:

options.a: Refraction of light through air layers of different temperatures

questions.explanation: Mirage = light bending through hot air near ground.

questions.questionText: 100°C equals:
Substance with HIGH specific heat capacity:
questions.explanation: High SHC = more energy needed for ΔT = slow temperature change.

questions.questionText: Heat to melt 2 kg ice (Lf = 334 J/g):
Which has the HIGHEST thermal conductivity?
questions.explanation: Silver = highest thermal conductivity (metal, free electrons).

questions.questionText: Heat transfer rate depends on:
questions.explanation: Q/t depends on ΔT, area, conductivity.

questions.questionText: Higher R-value in building insulation means:
questions.explanation: Higher R = better insulation = slower heat transfer.

questions.questionText: Newton's law of cooling states cooling rate is proportional to:
questions.explanation: Cooling rate ∝ (T_object - T_surroundings).

questions.questionText: Sea breeze occurs during:
questions.explanation: Daytime: land heats faster → hot air rises → cool sea breeze blows in.

questions.questionText: A thermos flask minimizes heat transfer by:

options.a: Vacuum between double walls + silvered surfaces

questions.explanation: Thermos = vacuum (no conduction/convection) + silvered (low radiation).

questions.questionText: A black surface:

options.a: Absorbs more radiation than a shiny surface

questions.explanation: Dark surfaces = good absorbers AND emitters of radiation.

questions.questionText: V=12V, I=2A. Resistance =
Resistor color code helps determine:
questions.explanation: Color bands on resistor = resistance value in ohms.

questions.questionText: In series circuit with R1=4Ω, R2=6Ω, current through both is:
questions.explanation: Series: same current through all components.

questions.questionText: In a parallel circuit, voltage across each branch is:
questions.explanation: Parallel branches = same voltage as source.

questions.questionText: A 1000W device on for 3 hours uses:
questions.explanation: Energy = Power × time = 1000 W × 3 h = 3000 Wh = 3 kWh.

questions.questionText: If 1 kWh costs RM 0.30, using 100 kWh costs:
A circuit breaker differs from a fuse because it:
questions.explanation: Circuit breaker = resettable safety switch (vs fuse = one-time).

questions.questionText: In a 3-pin plug, the longest pin is:
questions.explanation: Earth pin is longest for safety (connects first/disconnects last).

questions.questionText: Standard earth wire color in Malaysia is:
questions.explanation: Earth wire = yellow-green striped (international standard).

questions.questionText: An electromagnet differs from a permanent magnet because:

options.a: It can be turned on/off with current
options.d: It is not magnetic at all

questions.explanation: Electromagnet = magnetic only when current flows.
